gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Gugi draws its verticals and horizontals at identical weight, a bold display heading whose lowercase nearly matches the capitals in height. Noto Sans Deseret's open apertures let paragraphs run without a snag.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-duployan: Distinctive and bold, Gugi cuts its terminals open so the counters flow outward, every glyph drawn with one simple tip. Noto Sans Duployan's oversized counters give the pair its greatest strength: generous openness.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Modern in feel, Gugi is drawn with no vertical emphasis and no horizontal thinning, its lowercase nearly reaching the capitals. Noto Sans Elymaic, an open-aperture sans, lets longer text glide along its low ascenders.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Stems and crossbars of matching thickness, with no hairlines anywhere, make Gugi a heading that looks drawn with a single tool. Noto Sans Ethiopic, a sturdy sans, gives the pair its backbone.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-glagolitic: Approachable round letters keep Noto Sans Glagolitic legible at small sizes, and the lowercase is sturdy. Gugi above it has no hairlines to squint at, so the heading stays crisp where the body takes over.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Noto Sans Grantha presses its small letters into flat pen-nib bowls, set under a true monoline Gugi heading. Noto Sans Grantha never snags on a closed-up bowl, so paragraph after paragraph glides by.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Crisp, chunky, hairline-free: Gugi has no thin strokes to squint at, while Noto Sans Gujarati ends its curves before they turn inward. Together, the bold heading and the sans-serif body stay open throughout.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Identical weight in every vertical and horizontal defines Gugi, a bold display heading. Noto Sans Hanunoo fills most of its height with lowercase and keeps its terminals open, a steady partner for that heading.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-hk: Gugi is bold, its crossbars matching the stems in thickness. Noto Sans HK, a sans with large lowercase forms and brush ends lifted before each curve closes, reads smoothly across a full paragraph.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-sans-imperial-aramai: Strokes of constant width, like bent pipe, shape Gugi, while Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic points the ends of its c apart. Their best trait is a bold heading over an approachable sans.
